mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Negative name clearance certificate (certificado de denominación social negativa), attached to the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance; authenticated by the Spanish notary at deed execution; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or incorporation certificate of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1954/1961 Convention) plus sworn translation (traducción jurada) into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity documents (valid passport or national ID) of all shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport authority of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for member states of the Apostille Convention; consular legalization for non-Convention states; Spanish consulate certification for periodic NIE filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special notarial power of attorney for incorporation formalities (poder especial para constitución)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary (if executed in Spain) or foreign notary with apostille
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille when executed abroad; direct notarization before a Spanish notary when executed domestically

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank KYC/AML onboarding dossier for the SL corporate account (UBO declaration, source of funds, PEP and sanctions attestation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish credit institution acting under Ley 10/2010 obligations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notary-certified copies or bank compliance-certified copies; secure video-identification accepted under SEPBLAC guidance; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EEAS), UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN (for USD transactions), and SEPBLAC high-risk jurisdiction parameters. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and their family members/close associates trigger enhanced due diligence, senior management approval and source-of-wealth verification under Art. 14 Ley 10/2010 and Art. 15 Reglamento 304/2014 when any relationship or transaction exceeds EUR 2,000. Continual transaction monitoring and annual re-screening are contractually required for Stripe/PayPal payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) in coordination with the Registro Mercantil Central online certification system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate denominations must be expressed in Spanish or any co-official language (Catalan, Galician, Basque) using the Latin alphabet. Foreign coined words (e.g., 'baby', 'maternity', 'supplies') are admissible if shown to be in common commercial use. The RMC applies a single-name identity rule: any denomination identical or phonetically/orthographically confusingly similar to an existing or reserved name is rejected, disregarding accents, punctuation and corporate form suffixes (SL, SRL).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A one-time extension of the reservation is available for an additional 90 days if the applicant re-files on the CIRCE/RMC portal before expiry. There is no formal administrative appeal against a negative name certificate; the applicant must promptly submit an alternative denomination on the same portal at no additional charge. If the denial is erroneous or a competing reservation is abusive, the applicant may file a recurso contencioso-administrativo before the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo in Madrid within two months of service of the RMC decision, or bring an unfair-competition action under Ley 3/1991 before the competent commercial court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital requires a real registered domicile where correspondence may be physically received and where management or administrative direction is based. A virtual office or registered agent address is accepted by the Mercantile Registry for incorporation and by AEAT for notification purposes, provided a physical reception and document repository exists. For ISIC 4791 e-commerce operations, tax residence follows effective management (Art. 8 Ley 27/2014, LIS), so a Spanish manager, tax representative or subleased co-working space is strongly recommended. Stripe, PayPal and acquiring banks require verifiable operating substance or at least a documented principal place of business before releasing settlement funds.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for standard-risk online retail: approximately 10% probability of an AEAT unannounced inspection or documentary verification within the first two fiscal years when turnover is below EUR 100,000 and declared sales reconcile with payment-rail volumes. Probability rises to above 30% once EU cross-border sales, VAT registration, significant refund claims or PEP/UBO complexity trigger SEPBLAC, AEPD or tax-audit oversight. No mandatory on-site inspection at incorporation, but notarial and registry verification of the registered address occurs at deed filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 20-22 (Incorporation), 58-60 (Capital), 62-63 (SL specific), 210-212 (Administrators).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) and the corresponding Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) where the registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Deed of Incorporation) and the corresponding application for registration (Inscripción) in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind. Capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name prior to notarization; the deposit certificate must be attached to the deed. No escrow account is required beyond this initial deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding members hereby subscribe to the entire share capital of the company, consisting of 3,000 shares with a nominal value of €1.00 each, fully paid up as required by law. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be established at Calle de la Infanta Mercedes 12, 28010 Madrid, Spain, within the jurisdiction of the Mercantile Registry of Madrid. RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as administrators: [Name] as Sole Administrator, with all powers granted by law and the Articles of Association. RESOLVED, that the administrators are authorized to execute all necessary documents, obtain the provisional tax identification number, and complete registration with the Mercantile Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIE) for Non-Resident Founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Consulate in the founder's country of residence or the National Police (Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras) in Spain.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form EX-15 (Solicitud de NIE) along with passport copy, proof of reason for application (e.g., incorporation of a company), and payment of the applicable fee (Tasa 790-012). If applying in Spain, schedule an appointment at the police station. The NIE is issued within 1-2 weeks.
required_dossiers: Completed Form EX-15
Valid passport (original and copy)
Proof of reason for NIE (e.g., draft deed of incorporation)
Payment receipt of Tasa 790-012 (€9.84 approx.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing documents within 10 working days. If the NIE is denied, appeal to the Dirección General de la Policía within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) – chosen by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft deed with the company name (obtain a negative name certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry), articles of association, capital details, and appointment of administrators. All founders must appear before the notary, either in person or via power of attorney. The notary will verify identity and legal capacity, then execute the deed. The notary will also handle the deposit of the capital certificate.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (Certificación negativa de denominación social) from the Central Mercantile Registry
Bank certificate of capital deposit (Certificado de depósito bancario) for €3,000
NIE or DNI of all founders
Draft articles of association (Estatutos sociales)
Power of attorney if any founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the deed, correct them and re-sign. If the name certificate is expired (valid 3 months), obtain a new one. If the bank certificate is insufficient, deposit the full capital and obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office or online via the electronic registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 working days after notarization, submit Form 036 (Declaración censal) to the AEAT to request the provisional NIF (CIF). The form must include the company's details, registered office, and fiscal representative. The provisional NIF is issued immediately or within a few days.
required_dossiers: Form 036 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores)
Copy of the notarized deed of incorporation
NIE of the administrator(s)
Proof of registered office (e.g., lease agreement or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected due to missing data, correct and resubmit. If the NIF is not issued within 5 days, contact the AEAT office or use the online system to track the status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located (e.g., Madrid).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, the provisional NIF, and the application for registration (Form 1) to the Mercantile Registry. The registry will review the deed for legal compliance and issue a registration certificate. This step is mandatory for the company to acquire legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (original and copy)
Provisional NIF certificate
Application form (Form 1) signed by the administrator
Payment of registration fee (approx. €100-200 depending on capital)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect (defecto), correct the deed or provide additional documents within the given period (usually 15 days). If the registration is denied, appeal to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish in the Official Gazette (BORME) and Obtain Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME) and AEAT.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the Mercantile Registry will publish the incorporation in the BORME (usually within 10 days). Simultaneously, the company must apply for the definitive NIF by submitting Form 036 to the AEAT, attaching the registration certificate. The definitive NIF replaces the provisional one.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Mercantile Registry
Form 036 (updated)
Provisional NIF certificate
Copy of the BORME publication (if available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is delayed, contact the AEAT. If the BORME publication is not issued, request a certificate from the registry. If the NIF is incorrect, file a correction with the AEAT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Social Security and Other Authorities (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and the local tax office (for economic activities tax).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the TGSS (if hiring employees) and obtain a social security number. Also, register for the Impuesto de Actividades Económicas (IAE) if the annual turnover exceeds €1 million (otherwise exempt). For online retail, no special license is required, but if a physical warehouse is used, obtain a municipal operating license (licencia de apertura).
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Mercantile Registry
Definitive NIF
Form TA.6 (employer registration) if applicable
IAE registration form (if applicable)
Municipal license application (if physical premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS rejects the registration, correct the data and resubmit. If the municipal license is denied, appeal to the local council or provide additional safety documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – online retail of maternity and infant supplies does not require industrial licensing under Spanish law. The Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism (Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo) oversees general commercial activities but no specific permit is needed for e-commerce.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no industrial or manufacturing permit is applicable. If a physical warehouse or office is used, a municipal operating license (licencia de apertura) may be required, but this is not a statutory industrial license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) – Environmental assessment is not required for online retail activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is classified as a non-polluting service activity under Annex II of Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment. No EIA report or registration is needed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC emissions, or waste handling beyond standard municipal waste. If a warehouse is used, compliance with local waste management regulations (e.g., separate collection of packaging) is required, but no specific discharge standards apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificado de protección contra incendios) is required only if physical premises are used, in accordance with the Technical Building Code (CTE) and local fire regulations. Structural load inspections are not applicable for office/warehouse use unless the building is subject to special conditions. Workplace clearance (acta de inspección) from the labor authority may be required if employees are hired, ensuring compliance with occupational health and safety standards (Law 31/1995).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign shareholders must first obtain a Spanish NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) via the Spanish consulate or AEAT police registration. The Spanish SL is then incorporated by notarial deed and registered in the Mercantile Registry; AEAT assigns a provisional NIF (CIF) through Form 036 before operations begin. Once the company is formally registered, the definitive NIF is issued. A non-resident legal representative with tax residence in Spain must be appointed if the entity has no permanent establishment or local management office. For recurring cross-border e-commerce sales, the Spanish SL should register for IVA immediately, using Form 036 or the AEAT electronic registry, and, if applicable, for the OSS (One-Stop Shop) scheme.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Spain. A Spanish SL is a resident corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide income. Available statutory options include: (i) election to file as a consolidated tax group under articles 61-75 of Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades when common control requirements are met; (ii) optional application of the Spanish foreign branch exemption model for non-resident operations; (iii) no domestic hybrid mismatch election—ATAD rules in anti-hybrid legislation apply mandatorily to cross-border arrangements; and (iv) the OSS registration election for intra-EU distance sales and certain cross-border B2C services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) / Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold; any person carrying out economic activity in Spanish territory must register for IVA before making initial taxable supplies. For intra-EU distance sales of goods, the OSS annual threshold is EUR 10,000 for cross-border B2C turnover (below that threshold, Spanish IVA applies unless opt-in; above it, destination-state VAT applies). Special simplified VAT regimes apply to small retailers with prior-year annual turnover below approximately EUR 150,000, but IVA registration remains mandatory for the Spanish entity in all cases.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates electronic invoicing (Facturae or other structured formats) for B2B transactions under Ley Crea y Crece and Royal Decree 1008/2023, phased in from July 2025 for large taxpayers with turnover above EUR 8,000,000 and from July 2026 for smaller businesses. In the Basque Country, TicketBAI requires near-real-time IVA transaction reporting through authorised billing software with digital signature and QR verification. The AEAT SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) regime obliges larger taxpayers and registered VAT groups to report invoice details electronically within 4 or 8 days. No fully national real-time fiscal clearance API applies to all SMEs, but export operations require AEAT-accepted electronic customs declarations and invoice records in the SII format if turnover exceeds the statutory thresholds.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Spanish IVA treats exports of goods to non-EU destinations as exempt with deduction of input VAT (effective 0%). The seller must prove that the goods physically left EU customs territory within 3 months of the supply. The buyer must be located outside the EU and the goods must be dispatched or transported by the seller, the buyer, or a third party on their behalf. For services and certain ancillary e-commerce logistics, 0% applies when the recipient is established outside the EU and the service is effectively consumed abroad. For intra-EU B2B supplies of baby/maternity products, zero-rating is available only if the customer provides a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are transported to another EU member state, supported by the Article 32 UVA exemption evidence. Sales to EU consumers above the OSS threshold are taxed at the destination state's VAT rate, not 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / DAU) accepted by AEAT
Bill of Lading or equivalent international transport document (CMR, air waybill, postal or courier proof of dispatch) evidencing physical exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer/foreign exchange records substantiating receipt of payment from outside the EU
Commercial invoice showing the goods value, HS codes, INCO terms, and destination buyer details
For intra-EU B2B supplies: the customer's valid EU VAT number and the periodic EC Sales List (modelo 349) filing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exports must be documented and retained for the statutory 4-year limitation period. If AEAT determines that the zero-rating was applied without sufficient proof of export or that the goods never left the EU, the full 21% IVA is immediately assessed plus late-payment interest from the due date. Deliberate or materially false zero-rating claims constitute a serious tax infringement under Ley General Tributaria, attracting penalties of 50% to 150% of the tax loss; cases involving unjustified offsetting or false transportation documents can reach 200%. When the IVA amount exceeded EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud charges under article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code may apply. AEAT also scrutinises cross-border reimbursements for unrepatriated funds or related-party pricing; invalid export substantiation triggers retrospective clawback of IVA refunds claimed on the export transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) and the Dirección General de Transacciones Internacionales (DGTI) under the Ministry of Economy, Commerce and Business, with oversight from the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible. Current account transactions (including trade in goods and services) are unrestricted. Capital account transactions are generally liberalized under EU law, but certain reporting obligations apply for statistical and tax purposes. Profit remittance is permitted without prior authorization, subject to corporate tax compliance and anti-money laundering (AML) verification. No material hurdles for a standard e-commerce entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds for euro-denominated receipts. For foreign currency receipts, there is no statutory timeline for conversion; entities may hold foreign currency accounts. However, all cross-border transactions exceeding €10,000 must be reported to the Banco de España for statistical purposes (via the 'Declaración de Transacciones' form). No mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account for business operations)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Spain recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., from UK or other EU states) can passport into Spain, but they must be registered with the Banco de España. For a low-risk e-commerce entity, EMIs like Wise or Revolut Business are viable for ancillary transactions, but a domestic bank account is recommended for primary treasury operations to ensure full SEPA and SWIFT integration and to avoid potential restrictions on inbound capital from non-EU jurisdictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not strictly mandated for SL directors if the entity is already incorporated in Spain. Remote onboarding is permitted under Spanish AML law (Ley 10/2010) provided that the bank uses video identification and electronic verification. However, for non-resident directors, a physical visit or a notarized power of attorney may be required by some banks. For a Spanish SL with resident directors, remote opening is generally accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with high-risk jurisdiction nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Certified passport copies and proof of address; (2) Corporate registry extract (Registro Mercantil) showing UBO structure; (3) Source of funds declaration with bank statements for the last 6 months; (4) Business plan and pro-forma invoices to demonstrate legitimate e-commerce activity; (5) Tax identification numbers (NIF) for all UBOs; (6) If applicable, a legal opinion from a Spanish attorney confirming the legitimacy of the corporate structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volume in early stage without established credit history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Signed contracts with major suppliers or marketplace agreements (e.g., Amazon, Shopify); (2) Historical payment processing statements from Stripe/PayPal; (3) A detailed cash flow forecast; (4) Corporate bank reference letters from any existing financial institution; (5) Evidence of compliance with GDPR and consumer protection laws.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between declared business scope and actual payment flows (e.g., large inbound transfers from unrelated third parties)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) A comprehensive list of expected counterparties with their legal status; (2) Copies of commercial contracts or purchase orders; (3) Explanation of any third-party payments with supporting documentation; (4) Commitment to maintain transaction-level records for 5 years as per AML obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For capital injections from non-resident shareholders, use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'G2' (Direct investment) or 'C1' (Capital transfers) under the Balance of Payments classification. The transfer must be accompanied by a 'Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores' (Foreign Investment Declaration) filed with the DGTI within one month of the transaction if the amount exceeds €3,000,000 (or for any amount if the investor is from a non-EU tax haven). For amounts below this threshold, a simplified post-hoc declaration is required. The bank will verify the corporate resolution and the NIF of the receiving entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (e.g., purchasing inventory from China or Latin America), use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for larger transactions. Spain is a member of SEPA, so euro-denominated payments to EU suppliers are processed via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with IBAN and BIC. For non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is the standard. Ensure compliance with EU sanctions and export controls; no specific clearing rail restrictions apply for maternity supplies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Forwards (deliverable) on EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/MXN, and other major currencies
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., certain LatAm currencies) if the underlying exposure is non-euro
Currency Swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for long-term balance sheet hedging
FX Options (plain vanilla) for risk management, subject to bank approval and ISDA documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Accounts Deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Provincial Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities: financial statements must be prepared by 31 March, approved by the shareholders' meeting by 30 June, and filed within one month of approval (standard deadline: 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 plus mandatory monitored reminder process; repeated non-filing may lead to closure of the registry sheet and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax Return - Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days after the six-month period following the tax year close (calendar year: 1 August; standard calendar-year deadline: 25 July; the 25th is the final day).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers surcharges of 5%-20% plus late-payment interest; penalties range from EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 per missing data item or EUR 1,500 plus 50% of the tax liability for false submissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 - Declaración de Operaciones con Terceras Personas (Annual Third-Party Transactions Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually for the preceding calendar year, due between 1 February and 31 March, provided transactions with a single counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing with omissions results in penalties from EUR 150 to EUR 20,000; systematic non-compliance can lead to tax records audit and possible suspension of tax benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Actualización de Titularidad Real (Beneficial Ownership Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not an annual recurring filing; mandatory only upon acquisition, transfer, or alteration of significant shareholding or BO status, within 30 calendar days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing leads to negative certificate issuance (certificación negativa), registry suspension, and potential fines under anti-money laundering law (Law 10/2010) of EUR 600 to EUR 60,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent age audit if at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets > EUR 2,850,000; net turnover > EUR 5,700,000; average headcount > 50. Exemption is lost if the same thresholds are reached in the second consecutive year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable – PGC) for individual annual accounts; EU-adopted IFRS for consolidated accounts of groups when required; small and medium enterprises may use abbreviated PGC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation. Beneficial ownership information is registered with the Commercial Registry upon incorporation and updated within 30 days of any share transfer or BO change. The annual accounts filing does not require a separate BO declaration unless substantive ownership changes have occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas (Minute Book for Board and Shareholder Meetings)
Libro Registro de Administradores o Consejeros (Register of Directors)
Libro Diario y Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Accounting Books required under the Commercial Code)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created Spanish SLs engaged in an economic activity pay a reduced 15% rate on the first €300,000 of tax base (25% on the excess) for the first two profitable tax periods. R&D and technological innovation deductions (up to 42% of qualifying R&D expenses and 12% for technological innovation) may further lower the effective burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return); mandatory electronic filing via Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (plus quarterly prepayment filings on Form 202)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days after the expiry of six months following the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, by 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF, legal name, tax domicile, and fiscal year start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL must complete this using its Spanish NIF; non-resident shareholders are not entered on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation: accounting profit, statutory adjustments, and offset of prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Spanish entity's profit and loss attributes are included; non-resident shareholders' income streams are not included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability before credits, after applying the standard 25% rate or the reduced 15% regime for newly created companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the entity-level rate; no non-resident allocation is made on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, withholdings, quarterly installment payments already made, and final tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Includes only amounts withheld from or prepaid by the Spanish SL; dividend withholding paid to the tax administration is not reduced by this return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without AEAT notice triggers a surcharge of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6 months), 15% (within 12 months), or 20% (after 12 months) of the net tax due, plus late-payment interest. If filed after a formal inspection notice, the surcharge is 20% plus interest. A minimum fixed penalty of €200 applies for late submission when no tax is owed; false or omitted data may attract penalties of 50% to 150% of the assessed shortfall.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (withhold at source on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, unless EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable tax treaty reduces the rate).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must deliver an authenticated Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) covering the relevant fiscal year to the Spanish SL before payment. The SL then applies the reduced treaty rate or the 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive rate if the minimum 5% shareholding and 12-month holding period are evidenced. If excess WHT is withheld, the non-resident may file for a refund with AEAT using Form 210/211 within the statutory period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 19% on royalty income and 19% on interest income paid to non-residents. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, 0% withholding applies for associated EU/EEA companies meeting the ownership and holding-period tests. Bilateral tax treaties typically reduce rates to 0–15% for interest and 0–10% for royalties depending on the jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 per transaction category of annual related-party operations triggers the Local File; Master File and Country-by-Country Report are triggered at EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) framework in the offshore sense, but Spanish GAAR (LGT Article 15), ATAD-based CFC rules, and CIT anti-abuse doctrine require real economic substance: physical premises, payroll, local management, and operational decision-making. A Spanish SL without genuine substance faces recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, and reallocation of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating online sales, issuing false invoices/chargebacks, recording fictitious supply-chain costs, or failing to declare payments received through Stripe/PayPal rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the evaded tax plus late-payment interest. If the evaded amount exceeds €120,000 per tax period, criminal fraud consequences apply: imprisonment from 1 to 6 years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally and severally liable under LGT Articles 42 and 43 for assessed taxes, surcharges, and interest when the company becomes insolvent as a result of their fraudulent conduct. Criminal conviction may also trigger imprisonment, passport/travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal Spanish SL with no employees, premises, inventory control, or genuine management activity solely to shelter profits, access tax advantages, or claim digital-nomad benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may disregard the legal entity, reallocate its income to the actual beneficial owner, deny all deductions and treaty benefits, and impose penalties of up to 150% of the recomputed tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced for fraud or abuse; directors and shareholders risk unlimited liability for the full tax debt and criminal responsibility if the shell was used to commit tax evasion or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Cross-Border Payment Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the e-commerce business without proper customer due diligence, ignoring unexplained payment flows through Stripe/PayPal, failing to file beneficial-ownership statements, or omitting suspicious activity reports required under Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Serious AML violations carry fines of €60,001 to €150,000; very serious violations carry fines of €150,001 to €600,000 or up to 25% of the transaction amount if higher. Criminal money laundering is punishable by imprisonment from six months to six years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face individual fines, professional disqualification, criminal liability for money laundering, and possible travel restrictions or bail conditions while proceedings are pending.
